## Learning goals

By the end of this week, you should understand:

- why web data can provide valuable marketing or consumer insights;
- how a research question, a data source, and a data-collection method need to fit together; and
- which methodological, technical, and legal trade-offs shape a web data project.

## Lecture

The lecture introduces web data as a research resource and provides frameworks for designing web data projects. It uses the following readings:

::: {.callout-note title="Readings"}
The papers below provide guiding frameworks for the rest of this course, and chance is you'll have to read it a couple of times (e.g., first to get an overview, and later to appreciate and use the details in your project). 

- ["Fields of Gold: Scraping Web Data for Marketing Insights"](https://doi.org/10.1177/00222429221100750) 
- ["Unlocking the potential of web data for retailing research"](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jretai.2024.02.002)

Note: The web appendices contain valuable tables, so do not skip them.

:::
